newsitems.title: Screenshot Competition – Beyond Repair!
newsitems.author: Blitzkrieg Wulf
newsitems.contents:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/d66fbf64694823ff8108572f51a5f97fb097c0db.png[/img]

[h1]Welcome to the 248th War Thunder Steam Screenshot Competition![/h1]

Thanks for all of your amazing screenshots last week! This week, the competition is focusing on the aftermath of dogfights, town skirmishes, and battles on the high seas! Capture the moment of victory with a damaged or destroyed vehicle in your screenshot. Happy Halloween! The three most popular and three selected by us will get 300 GE. See the winners down below!

[h2]Let’s begin the 248th edition of our competition![/h2]

Create a stunning screenshot and submit it on the War Thunder Steam Community Hub with the tag [b]#WTscreen248[/b]. You have time until the [b]6th of November[/b] to submit your screenshot.

After that date, 6 winners will be selected (3 of which will be the highest rated by the community and 3 selected by our judges), each of which receive a reward of 300GE.

[h1][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3439537726 style=button]How to Participate![/url][/h1]

[h3]Terms:[/h3]
[list]
[b][*] Your screenshot must feature damaged or destroyed player vehicles.
[*] You must add the #WTscreen248 tag (title cannot have any other text in it).
[*] Artists may only win by popular vote once per four screenshot competitions.[/b]
[*] Screenshots need to be compliant with the War Thunder rules.
[*] You need to be the author of the screenshot.
[*] Screenshot needs to be new. You cannot use those which have previously been published or used in other competitions.
[*] We will only accept raw screenshots from the game. You cannot use any editing software nor any other visual enhancements (like Nvidia Ansel filters).
[*] You can use filters and settings built into War Thunder.
[*] You can use the replay functionality built into War Thunder.
[*] Rewards will be delivered to the author's account within 14 working days.
[/list]

[h2]And now, time for the winners of the competition’s 247th edition – Haunting Grounds![/h2]

[h3]Winners selected via community votes:[/h3]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3826968353
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3826967524
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3827276494

[h3]Winners selected by our judges:[/h3]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3828843493
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3827223646

Each winner will get 300GE! Congratulations and see you next week!

newsitems.title: Leopard 2A8: A Coveted Trophy
newsitems.author: Blitzkrieg Wulf
newsitems.contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/dae00f3a845f9f9d201e7795b267b948a470b86b.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Introducing the Leopard 2A8, Europe’s most advanced tank and the first mass-produced Leo equipped with an active protection system![/p][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p][b]Leopard 2A8: [/b]An MBT for Germany and Sweden at Rank VIII[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]At a glance:[/p][list][*][p]Trophy Active Protection System[/p][/*][*][p]DM53 APFSDS[/p][/*][*][p]Good level of protection[/p][/*][*][p]GEN 3 thermal imagers[/p][/*][/list][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/af0eca476f34a689f826b0eb56317df9b7b3e75e.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Introducing the Leopard 2A8[/b][/h3][p]Today we’re excited to be showing you the Leopard 2A8, coming in as one the most advanced MBTs in War Thunder! Its defense is bolstered by a new protection system, making it stronger than ever. Read on to find out more about how this thing performs![/p][p][/p][h3][b]Using the Leopard 2A8 in Battle[/b][/h3][p]The Leopard 2A8 represents the pinnacle of the Leopard 2 MBT family and serves as a direct successor to the Leopard 2A7 variants already featured in the game. This variant has been designed to address the challenges of the modern battlefield and incorporates the Israeli Trophy active protection system (APS) for outstanding defense against guided missiles.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/8a4472b4c4d74e77cb41bbbd743d6f7659529e17.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/475e1266ea6d3900d6d77dbe7cf45b9abb711893.jpg"][/img][/p][p]It’s heavy, but is also well-armored and is equipped with advanced electronics and a long-barreled cannon. Its stock APFSDS round has great penetration power, however once the superior DM53 APFSDS round is unlocked, the Leopard 2A8 can penetrate almost any part of the strongest opponent on the battlefield! While its mobility is somewhat reduced compared to the more agile 2A4 and 2A5 models, it remains highly competitive in top-tier combat. The tank features an internal spall liner and additional frontal hull armor, while the side protection has been bolstered with extra composite armor modules. Combined with the new APS, these upgrades provide excellent protection against anti-tank guided missiles launched from ground vehicles or aircraft.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Feature Spotlight: Trophy APS[/b][/h3][p]We’re sure that you’ll all be familiar with the Israeli Trophy active protection system, as it’s found on the Merkava Mk.4M and M1A2 (Trophy-HV) tanks. For those who don’t know, the Trophy system alerts you to an incoming missile and automatically intercepts it using countermeasure projectiles positioned around the turret. There are 6 charges available, providing the tank with all-around protection against ATGMs, whether launched from the ground or air![/p][p][/p][p][b]Developer comment: [/b]The Leopard 2A8 serves as a logical evolution of the 2A7 variant. In the Eagle’s Shadow major update, the vehicle will be introduced for two nations: Germany and Sweden, with the latter receiving the Leopard 2A8 variant configured for the Norwegian Army. The most significant new feature is an Active Protection System, which provides an enhanced level of defense, primarily against helicopters, as well as ground-based ATGM launchers. With the Leopard’s survivability bolstered even further, all that remains is to put it to the test in battle![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/833d9f541a325035c83ccddd4567ba30a48d2725.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Vehicle History[/b][/h3][p]In February 2023, the Norwegian Defense Materiel Agency (Forsvarsmateriell) signed a contract with KMW for 54 Leopard 2A7+ tanks for Norway, with deliveries scheduled for 2026–2028. In June 2023, the parties agreed to amend the contract to specify the Leopard 2A8 variant; these tanks were designated as Leopard 2A8NO. In May 2023, the German Federal Office of Bundeswehr Equipment, Information Technology and In-Service Support (BAAINBw) concluded a framework agreement with KMW for 123 Leopard 2A8 tanks for Germany.[/p][p][/p][p]On November 19th 2025, the first production-standard Leopard 2A8 and 2A8NO tanks manufactured for Germany and Norway, respectively were unveiled at the KNDS Deutschland testing ground in Munich. Furthermore, plans are in place to supply Leopard 2A8 tanks to Lithuania, Sweden, the Netherlands, the Czechia, and Croatia.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/6c3afb2c930bdec5cd809e9232956d75fb097d7c.jpg"][/img][/p][p]That’s it for this one, the Leopard 2A8 is set to be one of the strongest MBTs in the game thanks to its strong armor and APS. See you in the next dev blog![/p][p][/p][p align="center"][i]Please note that vehicle specifications may be subject to revision and change before being added to the game.[/i][/p]

newsitems.title: Improving Tank Mobility Mechanics: New Steering Mechanisms & Engine Refinements
newsitems.author: Blitzkrieg Wulf
newsitems.contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/7dc510e69c40a9d21436b484e89c6c2b616ce4e0.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Hi everyone! We’re continuing to refine mechanics related to vehicle mobility. Some of these will significantly alter how vehicles behave, making them more effective in certain situations while less so in others. We’ll introduce these on the dev server so that you can try them out. Other mechanics will improve vehicle performance regardless of the situation, and we plan to release these alongside the Eagle’s Shadow major update.[b] [/b]Let’s dive in.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Mechanics Undergoing Testing[/b][/h3][p]The dev server will feature mechanics for the steering systems of tracked vehicles, designed to bring their behavior closer to that of real-world counterparts. These include the double-differential steering mechanism, which we previously tested on a previous dev server, as well as dual transmission and planetary (epicyclic) gear mechanisms.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Double Differential[/b][/h3][p]Let’s start with the theory. In vehicles equipped with a double differential mechanism, a portion of the engine’s power is transmitted to the tracks via the gearbox, while another portion is routed through a differential steering mechanism. The final torque applied to the half axle, which drives a track, is the result of combining the torque delivered through the gearbox with the torque transmitted through the differential mechanism that slows one half axle down while speeding the other one up. This configuration makes it possible to slow down one track while using the “saved” energy to accelerate the other.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/a3011325269b4255237949263e7be3b58909f336.jpg"][/img][/p][p][url="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:AndrewDressel"][u][i]AndrewDressel[/i][/u][/url][i], [url="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Differential_steering_mechanism.png"][u]Differential steering mechanism[/u][/url], licensed under [url="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode"][u]CC BY-SA 4.0[/u][/url], via Wikimedia Commons[/i][/p][p] [/p][p]In a double differential mechanism, there is no fundamental difference between turning while in motion and pivoting in place; both maneuvers mechanically function in the same way. When the transmission is in neutral, torque is transmitted solely through the steering mechanism, causing the axles to rotate in opposite directions, which is what enables a vehicle to turn in place. Consequently, for tanks equipped with a double differential steering system, the pivot speed will change with the addition of the new steering mechanic, and for some vehicles, the time required to complete a pivot may increase.[/p][p][/p][p]One aspect of this design is that the turning radius is larger than that of vehicles equipped with a side gearbox or planetary steering mechanisms; it depends on the difference in rotational speed between the two axles. However, the maximum rotational speed of the differential is limited, and the maximum rotational speed of the transmission’s output shaft varies depending on the selected gear. As a result, while the maximum absolute difference in axle speeds (in terms of RPM) remains constant, the ratio of these speeds depends on the gear currently engaged. Therefore, the minimum turning radius increases based on the gear in which the vehicle is moving. For instance, in the M1A1 Abrams tank, the calculated turning radius varies according to the gear as follows:[/p][p][/p][p]1 - 5.8 m (19.1ft), 2 - 11.3 m (37.1ft), 3 - 17.9 m (58.7ft), 4 - 26.9 m (88.3ft). [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/44d198c546207617fc48962ac956131ace032d7d.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]Edwards, J. and Brayer, R., AGT 1500 Powerpack Improvement Project (M1 TMEPS), Vol. I, General Dynamics Land Systems for U.S. Army TACOM, Contract DAAE07-87-C-R006, March 1991, Table 5-2, p. 65. DTIC accession no. ADA234998.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]For a number of other tanks, the minimum turning radius at maximum gear can reach 30–40 meters, and sometimes even 70 meters. Therefore, tanks equipped with double-differential steering systems achieve a level of speed retention during turns that is unsurpassed among tracked vehicles at the cost of an increased minimum turning radius.[/p][p][/p][p]It should be noted that, due to their design, transmissions utilizing a double-differential steering mechanism lack the side clutches that would otherwise allow for the independent braking of a single track. Consequently, the independent braking of a track suggested by some players during the previous dev server session is fundamentally impossible for vehicles with double differential steering mechanisms.[/p][p][/p][p]However, following the previous test, we’ve implemented a downshift feature that triggers whenever the brake (or reverse key) is pressed while turning. This allows players to actively reduce their turning radius and gain better control over their vehicle.[/p][p][/p][p]You can test this mechanic on the Eagle’s Shadow major update dev server using M1 Abrams, Leopard 2A4, Leopard 2A8, Chieftain Mk.3, AMX-30 (1972), Challenger Mk.2, Type 90 (B) and Type 10. An up-to-date list can be found in the preliminary changelog for the dev server.  Please share your feedback with us.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Dual Transmission[/b][/h3][p]For vehicles equipped with dual transmission, such as the entire series of Soviet T series tanks and their derivatives, a fully functional steering mechanism has been implemented. In reality, these vehicles feature a separate gear box for each track; when turning, the transmission for the inner (slower-moving) track shifts into a lower gear, at most one step below the gear engaged for the outer track. This is now replicated in-game! Furthermore, the gear engagement can be partial, for instance, the sixth and seventh gears might effectively operate simultaneously, because the clutches are slipping. This results in a smooth, rather than stepped, turning motion.[/p][p][/p][p]However, the turning radius also depends on the ratio between the rotational speeds of the half axles. Consequently, when turning in “short” gears (those where the difference in speed between the gears is minimal) the turning radius can be quite large. For example, on the T-64 and T-72, the turning radius varies based on the selected gear as follows:[/p][p][/p][p]1 - 2.79 m, 2 - 6.04 m, 3 - 13.42 m, 4 - 13.93 m, 5 - 10.23 m, 6 - 10.1 m, 7 - 8.76 m.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/082b237dd2e7cb49ba413114a15bc0b52fc634fd.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]Source: Tank T-72A. Technical Description and Operating Instructions. Book One / Ministry of Defense of the USSR. — M. : Voenizdat, 1986. — Page 31 (original in Russian: Танк Т-72А. Техническое описание и инструкция по эксплуатации. Книга первая / Министерство обороны СССР. — М. : Воениздат, 1986)[/i][/p][p][/p][p]As can be seen, the turning radius in 3rd–4th gears is significantly larger than in 5th–7th gears precisely because of the “short” gears.[/p][p][/p][p]In contrast, the T-80’s side gearboxes utilize “long” gears (made possible by the installation of a gas-turbine engine), and the turning radii in the lower gears do not exceed those in the higher gears:[/p][p][/p][p]1st — 2.8 m, 2nd — 5.55 m, 3rd — 8.63 m, 4th — 8.86 m.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/b19feccf64864de814dd8ea862d194c86254dbf5.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]Source: Tank T-80B. Technical Description and Operating Instructions. Book One / USSR Ministry of Defense. — M. : Voenizdat, 1984 — Page 25 (original in Russian: Танк Т-80Б. Техническое описание и инструкция по эксплуатации. Книга первая / Министерство обороны СССР. — М. : Воениздат, 1984)[/i][/p][p][/p][p]However, it is worth noting that the turning radii specified in technical documentation are often theoretical, calculated solely based on the kinematic ratios of the transmission gears, and may not account for track slippage or the vehicle’s moment of inertia, both of which increase the actual turning radius.[/p][p][/p][p]The dual transmission, just like the double differential will have the downshift mechanic in turns which works when you brake. You can test the dual transmissions mechanics in the T-80BVM, T-72 (1989) and T-64B. An up-to-date list of vehicles can be found in the preliminary changelog for the dev server.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Planetary Steering Mechanisms[/b][/h3][p]The third type of steering mechanism involves the use of planetary (epicyclic) steering mechanisms. In reality, this mechanism engages a reduction gear on the inner (slower-moving) side to execute a wide-radius turn, while disengaging the clutch and applying the brake to execute a tight-radius turn. This design lowers speed loss during wide turns while still allowing for rapid, sharper turns, albeit at the cost of speed. In the game, this functions as follows: when initiating a gentle turn by short taps of the turn button or a minor deflection of the controller axis, a reduction gear is engaged on the inner side; conversely, if you attempt to turn while holding the turn key or deflect the controller axis a lot, the mechanism operates in the same way as it does on vehicles equipped only with simple side clutches (such as the T-34). When pivoting, however, the turn will always be conducted around the stopped track.[/p][p][/p][p]Unlike dual transmission or double differential steering systems, planetary steering mechanisms allow for independent braking of the left and right tracks, providing greater control. Furthermore, when a reduction gear is engaged, the turning radius remains constant regardless of the selected gear, as the speed ratio between the inner and outer tracks stays the same. However, these mechanisms do not compensate for the loss of speed that occurs during turns.[/p][p][/p][p]You can test the mechanics of planetary steering systems on a variety of vehicles. A complete list can be found in the preliminary patch notes for the dev server. The T-54 and T-44 serve as excellent examples for comparing vehicles with and without this steering mechanic.[/p][p][/p][p]While we plan to test double differential and dual transmission steering systems, they will not be included in this major update. The planetary steering mechanic, however, provided no issues arise, may be added in this update, as it enhances vehicle handling without imposing any trade-offs or drawbacks.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Torque Characteristics of Turboshaft Engines[/b][/h3][p]We are done with the steering mechanisms, let’s get to the changes in engines. To begin, let’s again look at some theory: as you may know, turboshaft engines are fundamentally similar to the jet engines used in aircraft. But turbojet engines use the resulting gas to propel the aircraft forward, while turboshaft engines use the resulting gas to move a separate, free (power) turbine, which then transmits the resulting torque to the tracks.[/p][p][/p][p]Unlike piston-based internal combustion engines, turboshaft engines produce immense torque at low rotational speeds (RPM). This happens because the rotational speed of the power turbine shaft is independent of the rotational speed of the gas generator’s turbine shafts, so the gas generator can operate at maximum power output even when the power turbine shaft is stationary or rotating at very low speeds. Under these conditions, torque is at its peak, and as the rotational speed increases, the torque decreases, which you can see on the graphs below.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/3122a8a9f5b4ea0b703613cfee2ffa75134df876.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Source: Honeywell International Inc., AGT1500 Turbine Technology: How to Be Quick and Smart, PA00-2613, May 2000, p. 2.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/30708c815df80c2b286a93df3f494db92c750d45.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/b794d4bee6588070544ca01ae86ae9b279657b16.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Before/After. The dependence of the torque and output power of AGT1500 on RPM. Green is torque, red is the output power.[/p][p][/p][p]This torque-to-RPM ratio allows for the use of transmissions with fewer gears. We have implemented an accurate full throttle performance curve (the dependency of torque on engine RPM) for turboshaft engines. Consequently, we’ll be removing the intermediate gears previously used on turboshaft-powered tanks, as these are gears that were originally implemented to emulate engine and transmission behavior in the absence of a rigid kinematic link between the tracks and the engine or gas generator. Thus, it will affect all tanks with torque converters and turboshaft engines.[/p][p][/p][p]Torque converters function in a similar way, increasing torque when the turbine wheel “slips” relative to the pump wheel. However, these are a topic for another time, as we plan to implement the torque converter mechanic in the upcoming updates.[/p][p][/p][p]Stay tuned for further details, share you opinion on the new steering mechanics and see you in battle![/p]

newsitems.title: New Modules for Ground Vehicles!
newsitems.author: Blitzkrieg Wulf
newsitems.contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/2eb486894f3ce86a5e2e8e2a1168dc2aec91346d.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]In today’s dev blog, we’re talking about new modules and features for ground vehicles![/p][p][/p][p]Hey everyone! In the next major update, ground vehicle players can look forward to new functional modules, more detailed damage models, and new capabilities for their favorite vehicles. Let’s take a look at everything![/p][p][/p][h3][b]Fire Control System (FCS) and Electrical Systems[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/f5c255437f86588ee61848fae1c17420f61dd4f8.jpg"][/img][/p][p]First up, you’ll notice new functional modules when using the X-ray view. The fire control system is now a distinct module that can be damaged or destroyed. If the FCS is disabled, the use of night-vision devices, thermal imagers and the rangefinder becomes unavailable. Furthermore, remotely operated machine-gun or cannon turrets that lack a manual aiming option will also be disabled.[/p][p][/p][p]Next is the new electrical system module, which is a critical component that powers the tank’s various systems. Disabling it shuts down a whole range of equipment that relies on power: the fire-control system, the gun stabilizer, radars, optoelectronic targeting systems, the threat-warning system, and even the autoloader. Make sure to learn the location of this module on all of your tanks (as well as your opponents, most importantly!), because a well-placed shot here will give you a massive advantage![/p][p][/p][h3][b]Manual Reloading for Tanks with an Autoloader[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/d458ba8f2bd7f5c97e3c83e87d9d88049c04f4ac.jpg"][/img][/p][p]In the next major update, we’ll be introducing a mechanic that will allow you to manually reload ammunition for tanks equipped with an autoloader. This will be available for tanks that have this capability in real life. So how does it work? Now, when the shells in the automatic loader are depleted or the autoloader is disabled, the crew will switch to loading the gun manually. If the loader is manually loading the gun however, the autoloader rack will not be replenished — you will have to stop firing for the loader to resume refilling it.[/p][p][/p][p]In the X-ray view in the hangar, you will be able to see the reload times for shells stored outside of the ready rack or the autoloader. The delay period before the ready rack begins to be replenished is also displayed. Additionally, the X-ray view shows the time required to replenish the autoloader or the ready rack. This provides a complete picture of how the loading system functions and highlights its weak points.[/p][p][/p][p]The new mechanic makes the behavior of tanks equipped with an autoloader more realistic and predictable. At the same time, it preserves tactical depth, because disabling the autoloader directly affects the rate of fire.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Auxiliary Power Unit[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/2ef3a0693836c9e3a589cd43bb47aa25114f27e6.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’re also adding an auxiliary power unit (APU) mechanic. Previously, if a tank’s engine was disabled and the battery was depleted, the vehicle would lose all power: the turret could only be traversed manually, aiming the gun became difficult, and all electronics would shut down. Now, many vehicles will have a “second heart” that keeps their electric systems operational, even if the engine has been destroyed.[/p][p][/p][p]The APU is implemented as a separate module that can be viewed in X-ray view. This allows you to see exactly where it is located on a given vehicle and how vulnerable it is. If an opponent destroys the power system, the APU will be unable to power the tank’s systems. Consequently, disabling the engine no longer results in an eventual total loss of power for the vehicle. However, keep in mind that the APU itself can still be rendered inoperable due to other types of damage. During combat, the APU can be switched off to prevent the noise of its operation from revealing your tank’s position.[/p][p][/p][p]It’s also worth noting that on many SPAAs and SAMs the APU is always working to ensure the functionality of power-hungry systems, such as radars, powerful FCS or aiming drives. These APUs will work constantly and disabling them would cause the power intensive systems to stop functioning.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s it for this one, we’ll be back soon with more information on the new mechanics related to turning and mobility of ground vehicles. Stay tuned![/p]

[p]Today we’re starting pre-orders for the American two-seater Hornet and the Chinese Q-5D attack jet aircraft![/p][p][/p][h2][b]F/A-18D[/b][/h2][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p][b]Pre-order - F/A-18D Pack[/b][/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/a2cb3a83ecfd61d4e0b0affdf113718ae35c8b50.jpg"][/img][/p][p]To get to the Gaijin Store through Steam, go to the in-game hangar > Shop > Online Store.[/p][p][/p][p]This pack includes:[/p][list][*][p]F/A-18D (Rank VIII, USA)[/p][/*][*][p]Premium account for 30 days[/p][/*][*][p]3000 Golden Eagles[/p][/*][*][p]Pre-order bonus: unique "Devilish Sting" title[/p][/*][*][p]Pre-order bonus: unique "VMFA-232 Red Devils patch" decal
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/ef5f20c6753d05782a6a8ed989748dfb7909a293.png"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]79.99[/b][/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p][b]F/A-18D: [/b]A Premium (Pre-order) Jet Fighter for the USA at Rank VIII[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]At a glance:[/p][list][*][p]Up to six AIM-120B missiles with active radar homing (ARH) seekers[/p][/*][*][p]Laser and satellite-guided precision-guided munitions (PGMs)[/p][/*][*][p]Excellent maneuverability[/p][/*][*][p]Moderate acceleration performance[/p][/*][/list][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/c48bdf07f815efb5ecb0b4360f29d86a1b259ad9.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Meet the latest addition to the Hornet family: the two-seat F/A-18D! This multirole jet fighter is set to become one of the best U.S. premium aircraft in the game, defined above all by its absolute versatility. With a massive arsenal of external stores and state-of-the-art avionics, pilots can fine-tune their combat machine for every specific mission. In an interceptor role, the F/A-18D can carry up to six AIM-120B active radar-homing (ARH) missiles, alongside weapons for closer-range engagements, such as the semi-active radar-guided AIM-7P and the highly maneuverable, all-aspect AIM-9M. Heading out for a ground-attack sortie? The F/A-18D offers access to some of the best air-to-ground ordnance available, including JDAM-ER and LJDAM-ER precision-guided bombs, AGM-65E Maverick missiles, and a wide variety of conventional bombs and unguided rockets. A hallmark of the series remains its exceptional responsiveness to flight controls, even at extreme speeds![/p][p][/p][p]The F/A-18D will arrive at rank VIII in the US aviation tree, where it will serve as a valuable addition to high-rank lineups across all game modes.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Q-5D[/b][/h2][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p][b]Pre-order – Q-5D Pack[/b][/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/e24abb3af98cab492c44f2a3f2d33c0f3d758011.jpg"][/img][/p][p]To get to the Gaijin Store through Steam, go to the in-game hangar > Shop > Online Store.[/p][p][/p][p]This pack includes:[/p][list][*][p]Q-5D (Rank VI, China)[/p][/*][*][p]Premium account for 15 days[/p][/*][*][p]2000 Golden Eagles[/p][/*][*][p]Pre-order bonus: unique title «Gambling Dragon»[/p][/*][*][p]Pre-order bonus: unique «The Flight of Dragon»
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/31aaa22788f5c8f4a899ed4b78d4d1a7e562cb74.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p]Pre-order bonus: unique camouflage «White»
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/84ec1fccc0090d0ed7171709faac9a42bb56be65.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][b]59.99[/b][/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p][b]Q-5D: [/b]A Premium (Pre-order) Strike Aircraft for China at Rank VI[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]At a glance:[/p][list][*][p]Increased number of hardpoints for unguided weaponry; capable of carrying up to 8 bombs[/p][/*][*][p]Supersonic[/p][/*][*][p]64 flares/chaff[/p][/*][*][p]Radar warning receiver[/p][/*][*][p]Good maneuverability[/p][/*][*][p]No air-to-air missiles[/p][/*][/list][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/970bb91d8c52b12bd33a486d0494d003458da6a6.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]In the game, the Q-5D serves as a further evolution of the Q-5 early and Q-5A models. It is a supersonic jet-powered strike aircraft featuring an increased number of weapon hardpoints and a capable ground-attack arsenal. The Q-5D excels in mixed-battle modes, its high speed combined with a payload of bombs and rockets supported by a ballistic computer allows for precise strikes followed by a rapid exit from the range of enemy air defenses. The new Q-5D is equipped with 64 countermeasures and an all-aspect radar warning receiver capable of detecting surface-to-air missile launches. However, as a dedicated strike aircraft, the Q-5D carries no air-to-air missiles, instead for air combat, it must rely on its high speed, excellent maneuverability (for a strike aircraft), and a pair of 23 mm cannons mounted in the wing roots.[/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]In terms of its capabilities, the new Q-5D sits between the earlier Q-5 and Q-5A variants and the more advanced Q-5L and A-5C. China now has a rank VI premium strike aircraft that fits perfectly into lineups at the 9.0–9.3 Battle Rating range, while also helping players research more advanced, higher-rank vehicles more quickly.[/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]You can pre-order the Q-5D and F/A-18D from today to get yourself some Golden Eagles, Premium Account time and pre-order bonuses![/p][p][/p][p align="center"][i]Please note that vehicle specifications may be subject to revision and change before being added to the game.[/i][/p]

newsitems.title: Custom Battle Rating for Aircraft: More Freedom For Your Vehicles!
newsitems.author: Blitzkrieg Wulf
newsitems.contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/c0a501cdda17a0e08c7218ed54df161b2c5b22c1.jpg"][/img][/p][p]What if your favorite aircraft could participate in battles at different Battle Ratings? You could use your familiar loadout at one Battle Rating, or equip more powerful weaponry and test your skills against tougher opponents.[/p][p][/p][p]Introducing custom Battle Ratings: a new mechanic where researching specific modifications unlocks additional Battle Rating options for the same vehicle. You decide which configuration to take into battle![/p][p][/p][h3][b]One vehicle, multiple Battle Ratings![/b][/h3][p]Certain types of weaponry significantly enhance a vehicle’s effectiveness and can have a decisive impact on its Battle Rating. But is it possible to use your favorite aircraft at a different Battle Rating with a different set of available weapons? Yes! This is precisely where the custom Battle Rating mechanic comes in.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/e98616cf5d66b25d9f9db018fc9069212b65c348.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/0cf6a38ce622e14818cc8958b746392b659cfaf9.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/cc0d6093ce4201fe5a66bc55ca776adc27596e43.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]Custom Battle Rating for the J-22M1A, as illustrated in the context of Air Realisitc Battles.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]An aircraft’s Battle Rating can now depend on its chosen loadout configuration, meaning a single vehicle may have multiple possible Battle Ratings. Once you research more advanced weaponry, you have a choice: you can either participate in battles at a higher Battle Rating, or remain at your current one. Researching a modification does not automatically force a change in your vehicle’s Battle Rating; instead, you decide which available options to equip in your hangar before heading into battle.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/a3b7a34fc865e5b0ed26e1f62b7b0551fb031697.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Even after researching the most advanced armaments, you can always return to a lower Battle Rating by simply opting not to use them. With premium vehicles, it’s even simpler: all modifications are unlocked upon purchase, allowing you to immediately start experimenting with different configurations for various Battle Rating ranges. Just imagine you research or purchase one aircraft, yet you end up with two or three different versions of that vehicle to take into battle at different Battle Ratings![/p][p][/p][p]How will this work? Let’s look at a few examples.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Tiger UHT[/b][/h3][p]Let’s take the German Tiger UHT helicopter as an example. Suppose its base configuration is assigned a Battle Rating of 11.0, while researching the PARS 3 LR missiles unlocks the option to play at a BR of 12.7. You will then have a choice: play at the higher Battle Rating, utilizing fire-and-forget missiles that allow you to retreat behind cover immediately after an attack, or return to Battle Rating 11.0, where these specific missiles are not available, but other air-to-ground guided missiles with semi-automatic or laser guidance remain available.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]MiG-21 Bison[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/5148689cc7ac9f45c8fa264279bc5794f30424d0.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This is a premium aircraft; all modifications are unlocked immediately upon purchase. Take a look at the various configurations possible for this same vehicle:[/p][p][/p][p]In its base configuration, which lacks active radar-homing (ARH) air-to-air missiles, the aircraft sits at a Battle Rating of 12.3. It is an excellent close-range dogfighter, equipped with a helmet-mounted display (HMD) for target designation and laser-guided bombs (LGBs). While advanced air-to-air missiles are unavailable, this allows you to employ the aircraft in a different role, within a different lineup, and against a different set of opponents.[/p][p][/p][p]Equip it with RVV-AE missiles, and you get a fighter with a Battle Rating of 13.3. The Bison can now engage targets beyond visual range using active radar-homing (ARH) missiles, while still retaining the entire arsenal from its previous configuration![/p][p][/p][quote][p][i][b]Please note: [/b]The indicated Battle Rating values ​​and armament options are provided as initial examples and may change during the development process.[/i][/p][/quote][p][/p][h3][b]When can we expect the new mechanic?[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/98ed6fca6c5c465bde97e4a268f9b7cf77165bb5.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We plan to introduce the first aircraft and helicopters with custom Battle Ratings in the very next major update. Initially, this new mechanic will apply to select aircraft models; you can find the full list in the update changelog. Any change to the Battle Rating will be clearly displayed when selecting a configuration, and any weaponry incompatible with that configuration will become unavailable.[/p][p][/p][p]In future updates, we are considering the possibility of applying the custom Battle Rating mechanic to ground vehicles, for instance, to certain top-tier tanks. But first, we’re beginning with aircraft.[/p][p][/p][p]We believe that custom Battle Ratings will open up new possibilities for your favorite vehicles. Explore weapons, try different configurations and find your playstyle in the most comfortable environment. What vehicle would you like to try at another Battle Rating? Share your thoughts in the comments. See you![/p]

newsitems.title: Pages of History (November): Incredible Luck
newsitems.author: magazine2
newsitems.contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/5e5284b85929b773bf599d99deb4dee3c3dcfc87.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="justify"]In Pages of History this month, you will find yourself at the center of events that took place in various theaters of war. From Italy and USSR, Egypt and Iran: participate in battles while using vehicles linked to these historic events and get some prizes![/p][p] [/p][quote][p]From November 1st until November 30th, you will be able to participate in 8 tasks consecutively. Completing each task will grant you a trophy with a reward, completing all of the tasks will earn you a unique profile icon! [/p][/quote][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/bb4254535dee7af33a71370d33887b197e441709.png"][/img][/p][h3]Robert Roland Stanford Tuck[/h3][p]Robert Tuck was one of the most successful British aces, credited with 27 to 29 aerial victories. While he flew the Spitfire for much of his career, he commanded No. 257 Squadron, which was equipped with the Hurricane until the autumn of 1941. Thanks to what became known as “Tuck’s luck”, he survived two mid-air collisions, four emergency parachute bailouts, and a long period of captivity in Germany after being shot down in January 1942. In February 1945, Tuck escaped from captivity alongside a Polish comrade who spoke Russian; upon encountering Red Army units, the escapees joined them and, for a time, fought on the ground rather than in the skies! Fortune continued to favor Tuck, as he was eventually permitted to return to Britain, allowing him to celebrate Victory Day back home.[/p][p][/p][p]You can purchase this player icon for Golden Eagles until December 3rd (11:30 GMT) without completing tasks. To find it, go to your Nickname → Achievements → Pages of History.[/p][p][/p][h2]Trophy reward for each task[/h2][p align="justify"]Completing each individual task will give you a trophy with one of the following rewards:[/p][list][*][p align="justify"]20-50% RP booster for 3-10 battles[/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]20-50% SL booster for 3-10 battles[/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]3-5 universal backups[/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]Premium account for 1 day[/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]A random ground vehicle camouflage (out of those that can currently be unlocked or purchased with Golden Eagles)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]Other terms[/h2][list][*][p align="justify"]Tasks are available from 11:00 GMT until 11:30 GMT on the final day of each task.[/p][/*][*][p align="justify"]Tasks can be completed in random battles except for “Assault” mode.[/p][/*][/list][p align="justify"][/p][p align="justify"]You can read a detailed description of which task is for which day and check your overall progress by going to your Nickname → Achievements → Pages of History.[/p][p align="justify"] [/p][p align="justify"]November 1st — November 5th[/p][p align="justify"][b]Barbara Line[/b][/p][p align="justify"]Following the breach of the Volturno Line (the Wehrmacht’s first defensive position in central Italy) German forces conducted a gradual withdrawal toward their second line, the Barbara Line, over the course of three weeks. The terrain was well-suited for defensive operations, however, they were unable to hold the Barbara Line. On November 2nd 1943, Allied forces attacked the Wehrmacht’s fortifications and by November 3rd, had broken through them.[/p][p align="justify"] [/p][p align="justify"]November 5th — November 9th[/p][p align="justify"][b]The First Flight of the Hawker Hurricane[/b][/p][p align="justify"]On November 6th 1935, the Hurricane fighter, developed by Hawker Aircraft Ltd., took to the air for the first time. It became one of the most widely produced aircraft of the early Second World War, with a total of over 14,500 Hurricanes manufactured. These aircraft saw combat in Norway and France, defended Britain and Malta, were supplied to the USSR and Yugoslavia, and also served in the African theater of operations in their tropical variants.[/p][p align="justify"] [/p][p align="justify"]November 9th — November 12th[/p][p align="justify"][b]Battle of Taranto[/b][/p][p align="justify"]In the autumn of 1940, the main body of the Italian fleet was based in the city of Taranto, in the south of the country. To launch a surprise attack on the moored vessels, Great Britain concentrated its entire Mediterranean Fleet, and launched 21 Swordfish torpedo bombers from HMS Illustrious. The operation was highly effective: one Italian battleship was sunk, and two others sustained heavy damage. Great Britain seized the strategic initiative in the Mediterranean.[/p][p align="justify"] [/p][p align="justify"]November 12th — November 16th[/p][p align="justify"][b]Klinsko-Solnechnogorsk Defensive Operation[/b][/p][p align="justify"]In the autumn of 1941, the German offensive against Moscow ground to a halt due to deep mud. However, by November 15th the ground had frozen sufficiently to allow the advance to resume. Under the plan for Operation Typhoon, Moscow was to be seized in a pincer movement from the north and the south, but the Wehrmacht met with defeat in both directions. In the north, German forces captured Klin and Solnechnogorsk, only to be brought to a halt by December 5th. The Red Army then launched a counteroffensive, recapturing both towns by mid-December.[/p][p align="justify"] [/p][p align="justify"]November 16th — November 19th[/p][p align="justify"][b]Operation Crusader[/b][/p][p align="justify"]On November 18th 1941, the British Eighth Army launched its second offensive in Cyrenaica. It proved successful: for the first time in ground combat, the Wehrmacht suffered a defeat. Axis forces were compelled to retreat from Egypt into Libya, with a large number of their soldiers taken prisoner.[/p][p align="justify"] [/p][p align="justify"]November 19th — November 23rd[/p][p align="justify"][b]Operation Uranus[/b][/p][p align="justify"]On November 19th 1942, Soviet forces began the encirclement of Axis troops near Stalingrad. By November 22nd the ring had closed, trapping several hundred thousand soldiers. The German command recommended attempting a breakout, but Adolf Hitler forbade any evacuation, believing that the Luftwaffe would be able to establish an aerial supply line. This error proved fatal, as the encircled forces surrendered in early February 1943.[/p][p align="justify"] [/p][p align="justify"]November 23rd — November 27th[/p][p align="justify"][b]Formation of the “Normandie-Niemen” Fighter Regiment[/b][/p][p align="justify"]On November 25th 1942, an agreement was signed to form a French squadron on the territory of the USSR. In July 1943, the unit, named “Normandie” after a French province, was expanded to the size of a regiment; following its display of valor during battles near the Neman River in Lithuania, it was renamed “Normandie-Niemen”. In total, the regiment achieved 273 confirmed aerial victories.[/p][p align="justify"] [/p][p align="justify"]November 27th — November 30th[/p][p align="justify"][b]Operation Tariq al-Qods[/b][/p][p align="justify"]During Iraq’s 1980 invasion of Iran, Saddam Hussein’s forces captured numerous Iranian border towns, including Bostan. Attempts to retake them were unsuccessful for a long time; however, on November 29th 1981 during Operation Road to Jerusalem, Iran succeeded in recapturing the town, though at the cost of heavy casualties.[/p]

newsitems.title: Updated Sun City and American Desert and Improved Weather Settings!
newsitems.author: Blitzkrieg Wulf
newsitems.contents: [p]Today we’re taking a look at the updated Sun City and American Desert maps, plus improved weather settings![/p][p][/p][h2][b]Sun City[/b][/h2][p]Previously, when viewed from the air, Sun City resembled an oasis in the middle of a desert, isolated by surrounded sands. But that’s not how real cities are built, so we’ve decided to update it. Now, the entire location, including the aircraft areas, consist of a continuous urban landscape stretching along the coastline. You’ll be fighting in a proper, large-scale Middle Eastern city! The entire environment has been overhauled, from the buildings and vegetation, to the roads and vehicles. The streets have been brought to life with a wealth of smaller, detailed objects.[/p][p][/p][p align="center"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/244e5171b492c484ade74d4fec0d790a2ff676a9.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The new Sun City waterfront evokes a strong sense of déjà vu for those who remember the iconic games from the 2000s centered on criminal life in a sun-drenched resort town. Palm trees, the ocean, pink sunsets, and a faint hint of danger has now arrived in War Thunder![/p][p][/p][p]Before / After[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/06c9945849fc48507c7427949a561d4b1fc09af7.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/fcc867ab4ce6e221005292634e946d66a87c628d.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p]Before / After[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/f73946e9a1c4c7fb916742df9f6e56d1898eaf8e.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/fa67edc614e85b29c73752e82c3a1513366ac0f0.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p]The main new feature is the destructibility of the entire environment. If you crash into tiled walls, the tiles will fall away and all windows can now be shattered. Interiors have been added behind the storefront glass, for example if you see a building with a bank sign, you’ll see a bank interior inside, or if it’s a shop, you’ll see a retail space. Importantly, this destructibility does not alter the navigation of the map. You cannot create new paths in the walls of buildings, so tactical approaches remain unchanged.[/p][p][/p][p]Before / After[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/151b88bd1bcbd80090077a1c4b1a4ec741243cc0.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/e57ec276f4eb518fa683a0c5d0a3d167b86fb295.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p]Before / After[/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/2acbc57915f79e8ed7ac611c1a3f2002f223efa2.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/7eb61ee74a3588b23e0622d386fb9244b7724a7c.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p]Before / After[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/cb046b5300936c0674cc73f1369423df245d4c12.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/fd6bcf715ea9f519493578b7c6e12bab76f935fa.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][h2][b]American Desert[/b][/h2][p]American Desert is another map for Ground Battles that has undergone a complete environmental overhaul. We’ve paid particular attention to making the surrounding rocks and stones look as realistic as possible. Every building, tree, bush, road and minor detail has been reworked. However, all of the familiar routes and recognizable features of the map have remained in place, including the arriving train, which can still collide with any tanks in its path.[/p][p][/p][p]Before / After[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/3f3f9c0bf6a63323e62daa330af0b607f0f6cf38.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/a12162afb9aa89f110cfb23c2974f4f161d644f9.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p]Before / After[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/d18baccfe80d5438ddc85b8065582ccca5c637e1.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/ecbfa3bd1eb49843bcfd186ee56033dccf082cd6.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p]Before / After[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/ce863a7f1d1f4fee701ed5cbd9b37d21a0d747c4.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/f41a8a2067bc588202e4a4a756201904fb936ee6.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p]Both updated locations will appear in the game in the next major update, so be sure to check them out![/p][p][/p][h2][b]Improved Weather Settings[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]Before / After[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/d2708421a397ca7fdbe072a012aab86ba0ce3cf6.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/f1acccc20d14306f5ff0a1c336bbfe4c5337133d.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p]We’ve overhauled all of the weather preset settings! These changes apply to twelve presets in total, ranging from a serene clear sky, to a harsh storm. New cloud formations with more realistic shapes and density have been introduced, and lighting has been improved. Light now interacts with surfaces in different ways, depending on the selected weather preset.[/p][p][/p][p]Before / After[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/2b090743fb5497a28609c6e2f500e772473643ca.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/ceb1f5bf1d1c39042b5ce5f8ef340038ac93bb39.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p]“Clear” means a pristine, deep sky and sharp shadows that accentuate every detail of the surroundings. “Fog” cloaks the battlefield in a soft veil, blurring distant silhouettes and making the air feel perfectly still. “Thin cloud cover” streaks the sky with faint, subtle lines, barely altering the lighting. “Thunderclouds” grow heavy and leaden, heralding a storm and creating an unsettling atmosphere. “Rain” brings wet surfaces, glints of light on armor, and a distinct, ambient sound, while a “Storm” represents the climax: heavy clouds, intensified winds, torrents of water, and the sense that nature itself is intervening in the battle.[/p][p][/p][p]Before / After[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/87e7c16f8b4862cd1d21db6ddcf4d11e1af6f4de.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/0b6a7341ca1bbf4dd2bc3588919ee75ca94bac7f.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p]That’s it for this one folks! The main goal of this overhaul is to ensure that each setting aligns better with its name. All the updated weather settings will arrive in the game in the next major update. Stay tuned for more news![/p]

newsitems.title: Dreams Come True: Mistel 2 — Father and Son
newsitems.author: Blitzkrieg Wulf
newsitems.contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/71fb0b4e77235e5617b0f56209109c5b203834a6.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Mistel 2 was a German strike system built during the Second World War, consisting of a Fw 190 fighter acting as a carrier aircraft and a Ju 88 bomber, where the cockpit had been replaced by an explosive warhead![/p][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p][b]Mistel 2:[/b] A Premium Bomber for Germany at Rank III[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]At a glance:[/p][list][*][p]Unique two-aircraft design[/p][/*][*][p]3,500 kg warhead![/p][/*][*][p]No forward-firing armament[/p][/*][/list][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/571c18a75918503fc0b4fcb44c43b9cbdc8bd535.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Introducing the Mistel 2[/b][/h3][p]Meet Mistel 2, a very unique composite aircraft that can be obtained in the Dreams Come True event! This aircraft combines two aircraft together, where one drops the other as it acts like a bomb. Let’s take a look at how it works![/p][p][/p][h3][b]Using the Mistel 2 in Battle[/b][/h3][p]In combat, the Mistel 2 essentially functions as a bomber carrying a single, massive payload. The airframe of a twin-engine Ju-88G-1 was modified, replacing the cockpit area with an explosive shaped-charge warhead with a TNT equivalent of nearly 2,200 kg. Once the “bomb” (the entire aircraft) is aimed at its target, the carrier aircraft, the Fw 190A-8 fighter, releases the struts and connecting rod holding the bomber in place, allowing it to fly straight toward the target on autopilot. You’ll then have to return the carrier aircraft to an airfield to rearm the “bomb” (or in Arcade Mode, it reloads while in the air). Be careful though, as to save takeoff weight the Fw 190A-8’s own armament was removed, leaving the aircraft completely defenseless during flight. This does however make it very fast, allowing the carrier to potentially outrun enemies on the way back to the airfield. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/f8cfec56252967c22b565f873947cf909f849fe6.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/401acf8cc287037b5cc4285d9bef8929b273677b.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Feature Spotlight: The coupled-aircraft configuration[/b][/h3][p]Although the concept of two attached aircraft has appeared elsewhere in history, the Mistel 2 will be the first type in War Thunder! The primary goal behind this unusual configuration was to extend operational range and deliver the immense destructive power of a massive warhead. The entire assembly was controlled by a single pilot seated in the cockpit of the fighter aircraft. The large explosive charge, featuring a shaped-charge warhead, was intended for the destruction of warships, fortified structures, and critical strategic targets, such as bridges, power plants, and factories.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Developer comment: [/b]The Dreams Come True event is a great opportunity to add some truly unique military vehicles to the game. We’ve long considered implementing the Mistel system, and we are now thrilled to bring this unconventional strike platform to all War Thunder players. Developing the Mistel was an engaging challenge! We modeled the “bomb-aircraft” from scratch: it’s a Ju 88 G-1 with a completely redesigned nose section. For the Mistel configuration, we also had to modify the Fw 190A-8, removing its cannons and machine guns and creating a custom mounting system. Finally, we had to develop the mechanics for releasing the bomb-aircraft and guiding it toward its target, as nothing like this had existed in the game before. The result is a one-of-a-kind vehicle with its own distinct characteristics, and it’s easily one of the most unique machines in the game![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/6695806dca6b5ec89c9092e95a415a67177d1780.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Vehicle History[/b][/h3][p]The concept of composite aircraft was not a military innovation. These configurations had already been explored during the interwar period as a means to extend the range of passenger flights. In 1942, as Germany sought unconventional methods to counter the superior forces of the Allies, the idea was revisited. Engineers at Junkers proposed converting Ju 88 bombers into unmanned carriers for large explosive charges, with a manned fighter, either a Bf 109 or an Fw 190, mounted on top via special struts to control the entire assembly. The project was designated “Mistel” (German for “mistletoe”), though it was often jokingly referred to as “Father and Son”. The first flight took place in July 1943, and the results were deemed promising enough to launch a secret program codenamed “Beethoven”, carried out by the specialized unit KG 200.[/p][p][/p][p]During the war, several variants of the “Mistel” were developed, with a total of approximately 250 such units built. Their combat use was sporadic and failed to influence the course of the war. In June 1944, they were deployed for the first time against the Allied invasion fleet in Normandy; one attack damaged the British frigate HMS Nith, but no major vessels were sunk. A large-scale strike against the Soviet power plants supplying Moscow was planned, but it was ultimately canceled due to the rapid advance of the Red Army. The final instances of their use occurred during the defense of the Oder in April 1945, when they were employed against Soviet river crossings.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/c473e2b550562b9ad15866f68b080595d4faaa28.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The Mistel 2 can be obtained in the Dreams Come True event, which starts today! Check out the link below for more details.[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://steamcommunity.com/games/236390/announcements/detail/715667827053303815"][/dynamiclink][/p][p align="center"][i]Please note that vehicle specifications may be subject to revision and change before being added to the game.[/i][/p]

newsitems.title: IJN Takao: The Art of the Heavy Cruiser
newsitems.author: Blitzkrieg Wulf
newsitems.contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/32cc12acc895fd0c3727d4882a8b54beaf8adb33.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Japanese Takao-class cruisers are often described as the most well-balanced ships of this type in the service of the IJN.[/p][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p][b]IJN Takao:[/b] A Heavy Cruiser for Japan at Rank IV[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]At a glance:[/p][list][*][p]10 x 203 mm guns with a flat trajectory[/p][/*][*][p]High speed[/p][/*][*][p]Improved protection for ammunition magazines[/p][/*][*][p]Large number of automatic anti-aircraft guns[/p][/*][*][p]16 high-speed “Long Lance” torpedoes[/p][/*][*][p]Two seaplanes[/p][/*][*][p]Radar[/p][/*][*][p]Massive superstructure[/p][/*][/list][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/527e6cc1d75f06927f0c0d59383aa01f5b543087.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Introducing IJN Takao[/b][/h3][p]Today we’re excited to be looking at a swift, well-protected ship armed with ten 203 mm guns and renowned 610 mm “super-torpedoes”, coming to War Thunder in the next major update. Meet IJN Takao, an exemplary heavy cruiser![/p][p][/p][h3][b]Using IJN Takao in Battle[/b][/h3][p]Despite being a large ship, IJN Takao surprises with excellent speed for its class and features impressive ballistics from its ten 203 mm main guns. While IJN Takao’s armor can withstand hits from light cruisers, fire from large ships with large guns pose a serious threat. Given this, you’ll be much better suited for long-range engagements when using Takao, especially considering its lackluster secondary armament. However, for close-quarter encounters, Takao possesses an undeniable trump card: it has four torpedo launchers equipped with the renowned 610 mm super torpedoes, the finest of the Second World War! For defense against aircraft, Takao relies primarily on light anti-aircraft guns, featuring a total of sixty 25 mm automatic cannons. As an added bonus, Takao is equipped with an air-search radar and two catapults for seaplanes.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/1ca6c94b46ec38445a6be201d1300c1b12883966.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Feature Spotlight: A well-balanced heavy cruiser[/b][/h3][p]There are ships that have no glaring flaws, and IJN Takao is one of them. It performs well at both medium and long ranges, is effective whether operating solo or as part of a group, and boasts decent protection and survivability. While it has no firm drawbacks, no ship is perfect, as IJN Takao has some weaknesses, such as a massive, poorly armored superstructure and a very slow main battery turret traverse speed. Nevertheless, the well-balanced combination of its core combat characteristics easily outweighs these shortcomings. Takao is a fun and effective ship![/p][p][/p][p][b]Developer comment: [/b]Players will now have access to a ship that serves as a further evolution of the premium Myoko. In addition to ten long-range 203 mm guns housed in five turrets and excellent speed, IJN Takao features enhanced protection, particularly around the ammunition magazines, as well as a radar. On the downside, the ship has a larger profile and lacks strong secondary-caliber guns. Nevertheless, the new Takao is arguably set to become Japan’s best heavy cruiser.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/c04931ee2f85501c4dd31611d44c56e43fb8c625.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Vehicle History[/b][/h3][p]The design of this new class of cruisers began in 1925 under the direction of Kikuo Fujimoto, based on an improved version of the Myoko class. Although the Takao was the first to be laid down, its sister ship, the Atago, entered service two months earlier. At the time of the attack on Pearl Harbor, Takao was part of Vice Admiral Kondo’s 4th Cruiser Division, supporting the landings on Luzon.[/p][p][/p][p]In February 1942, the ship was based at Palau, where it intercepted vessels arriving from the Dutch East Indies; on March 1st, it sank a Dutch steamship and a British minesweeper. The following day, alongside Atago, it sank the American destroyer Pillsbury. On March 4th, it attacked a convoy near Cilacap, after which it returned to Yokosuka for the installation of additional anti-aircraft guns.[/p][p][/p][p]In April, Takao took part in the pursuit of the task force involved in the Doolittle Raid. In May, it rescued 471 crew members from the seaplane tender Mizuho. In June, it provided cover for the invasion of the Aleutian Islands. During the Battle of the Santa Cruz Islands, it joined other cruisers in sinking the aircraft carrier Hornet. In November, it participated in the bombardment of Henderson Field and sustained damage during an engagement with American battleships.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/9c2e0169f1d8b227eb2f96030ed4753ca529c0c7.jpg"][/img][/p][p]In early 1943, the ship supported the evacuation of Guadalcanal. In November, while at Rabaul, it was attacked by carrier-based aircraft and struck by two bombs; repairs were completed in January 1944. During the Battle of the Philippine Sea, Takao served as part of Kurita’s vanguard force. In October 1944, it departed from Brunei to take part in the Battle of Leyte Gulf, but while passing through the Palawan Passage, it was struck by two torpedoes fired by the submarine Darter. The cruiser lost all propulsion and was towed to Singapore. There, it was deemed beyond repair and repurposed as a floating anti-aircraft battery.[/p][p][/p][p]On July 31st 1945, British midget submarines attached six magnetic mines to its hull. The resulting explosion tore a hole in the ship. The cruiser remained afloat and continued to perform its duties until Japan’s surrender. After the war, its armament was removed, and on October 27th 1946, Takao was towed into the Strait of Malacca, where it was sunk as a target ship on October 29th.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s it for this blog! IJN Takao is set to be a strong contender for Japan’s best heavy cruiser. Until the next dev blog, happy sailing ahead![/p][p align="center"][i]Please note that vehicle specifications may be subject to revision and change before being added to the game.[/i][/p]

newsitems.title: Work-In-Progress: Freezing Daily Login Streaks
newsitems.author: magazine2
newsitems.contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/02c93e0045fcd872d91e06b629665f78be1a4d73.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Missed a day or two during a long login streak? That’s no longer a problem![/p][p][/p][p]Hey everyone! Today we’d like to tell you about a new mechanic that lets you freeze your daily login streak, preventing you from losing it. Let’s dive into the details of this mechanic, coming to War Thunder and War Thunder Mobile![/p][p][/p][h3][b]How does it work?[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/e9c59d4e585b36f592c2c07f6a9bfad5fd0027e4.jpg"][/img][/p][p]“Freezes” are earned by logging into the game. For every 12 days you login, whether consecutive or not, you’ll receive one “freeze” point. You can accumulate a maximum of 30 freeze points per account, which is enough to cover a month’s worth of missed logins over the course of a year. Each freeze point prevents your daily login streak from resetting when you miss a single day. The freeze is applied automatically the moment your streak would otherwise end; there’s no manual activation or confirmation needed. The system has your back! If you go without logging into the game for more days than you have freeze points, then your login streak will reset, but your freeze points will be preserved.[/p][p][/p][p]Your accumulated freeze points do not disappear. If you had 3 freeze points and were 8 days into the 12-day cycle before the next one and you didn’t log into the game for three years, you would still have those same three freezes on your return, with 9 remaining until the next freeze is earned. The counter simply continues to tick from exactly where you left off.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]For War Thunder and War Thunder Mobile[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/702420874854d1d2de6f056c2b0f87b7a3ce0df0.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The freeze mechanic for daily logins applies to both your War Thunder account and your War Thunder Mobile account. You’ll earn freeze points once per day by logging into either game. These points are only consumed if you have enough of them to cover the days missed in your login streak; they’ll be applied first to the game with fewer missed days.[/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]For example, if you have 8 freeze points, miss 3 days of your War Thunder login streak, and miss 10 days of your War Thunder Mobile login streak, the mechanic will use your freeze points to cover the 3 missed days in War Thunder. Your War Thunder Mobile progress will then be restored to the point it had reached on the day you last logged into War Thunder.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]It’s for everyone[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/10ae9caf475bc6bbe57abf857853afba0aa3d982.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This mechanic will be available for everyone and not linked to Premium account, everyone can use it without restrictions. You cannot buy or sell freeze points, as they are just an extra reward for logging in regularly, offering a bit of flexibility whenever you might need it. An indicator for your available freezes will appear on the daily login screen, so you’ll always know how many days you can skip.[/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]As soon as this new mechanic is ready to be implemented into the game, we’ll be sure to let you know![/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]That’s all for now! We’ll be back soon with more details on the next major War Thunder update, so be sure to stay tuned.[/p]

newsitems.title: Dreams Come True: Mistel 2
newsitems.author: Blitzkrieg Wulf
newsitems.contents: [p align="justify"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/7352fd8ae014eeef297cf7cb452b17b140ff13c1.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="justify"]Sometimes, things happen that you wouldn’t even dare to dream of. Meet the Mistel 2, a very peculiar aircraft(s!), featuring a Fw 190 literally carrying a Ju 88 bomb. Due to this unusual configuration, it earned the nickname “Father and Son”. By taking part in Air Battles, you can also earn a decal of the same name, a “Child with a Bomb” decal and a “Mistletoe” (the literal translation of “Mistel”) profile frame![/p][p align="justify"] [/p][quote][p]From October 28th (11:00 GMT) until November 11th (11:00 GMT), earn mission points in Air Battles, unlock stages and receive rewards![/p][/quote][p][/p][h2][b]Mistel 2: A Premium Bomber for Germany at Rank III[/b][/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/6695806dca6b5ec89c9092e95a415a67177d1780.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="justify"]The Mistel 2 is one of the most unusual strike systems in history. It consists of a combination of two aircraft: an Fw 190 A-8 fighter, stripped of its armament to reduce takeoff weight, and a Ju 88 G-1 bomber, the forward section of which was converted into a massive bomb equipped with a shaped-charge warhead. During flight, the pilot in the fighter’s cockpit would direct the bomber-aircraft toward the target; the attachments holding the two planes together would then be released, allowing the bomber-aircraft to fly toward its target in a straight line, guided by an autopilot.[/p][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,"][tr][td][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/0447212eba6c4bbd5761af275a870f7da017b936.png"][/img]  [/p][/td][td][p align="center"][/p][p align="center"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/67b5fb4dafbba5ed6f7b38c35ec65a1eccc05beb.png"][/img]     [/p][/td][td][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/831cdc2a5c5335f1f758be66a91cac5209920bc9.png"][/img][/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]“[b]Father and Son[/b]” decal[/p][/td][td][p]“[b]Child with a bomb[/b]” decal[/p][/td][td][p]“[b]Mistletoe” [/b]profile frame[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p] [/p][p]Among the rewards in the event is also this chest. When opened, there is a chance of receiving one of the following items:[/p][list][*][p]50,000 - 100,000 Silver Lions[/p][/*][*][p]Silver Lion and Research Point boosters[/p][/*][*][p]Random Wagers and Orders[/p][/*][*][p]Universal Backups (1 - 3)[/p][/*][*][p]A random camouflage for a vehicle you own[/p][/*][*][p]1 day of Premium Account[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2][b]How to get all rewards[/b][/h2][p]Each stage is unlocked for [b]35,000[/b] mission points and brings a new reward.[/p][p] [/p][quote][p][b]Please note: [/b]Once the stage is unlocked, you will need to claim your reward manually. To do this, click on your profile, select the “Dreams Come True: Mistel” category, and click Claim Prize.[/p][/quote][p][/p][p align="justify"]You’re able to earn mission points in [b]Air Battles[/b] at Rank III or above in Arcade, Realistic and Simulator Battles. The number of mission points to complete a stage depends on the game mode and the maximum Rank of the vehicle that you use in battle. There’s a multiplier for earning mission points, which is shown in the task description in-game.[/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]You can also earn mission points by using event vehicles that are Rank I and II. Event vehicles that can be used have the name of the event that they were obtainable in on their stat card.[/p][p] [/p][quote][p]Stages change every two days at 11:00 GMT: October 30th and November 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th.[/p][/quote][p align="justify"][/p][p]Rewards are given when you complete a specific number of stages[/p][list][*][p]For [b]1[/b] stage: one of the decal rewards[/p][/*][*][p]For [b]2[/b] stages: a trophy with a random reward[/p][/*][*][p]For [b]3[/b] stages: one of the decal rewards[/p][/*][*][p]For [b]4[/b] stages: a trophy with a random reward[/p][/*][*][p]For [b]5[/b] stages: [b]“[/b]Mistletoe” profile frame[/p][/*][*][p]For [b]6[/b] stages: the Mistel 2 premium aircraft[/p][/*][*][p]For [b]7[/b] stages: a special camouflage for the Mistel 2[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2][b]Discounts on purchasing stages using Golden Eagles[/b][/h2][p align="justify"]Incomplete stages can be purchased for Golden Eagles, but if you’re significantly close to completing a stage, its price will be significantly reduced.[/p][p][/p][p align="justify"]Let’s say you have earned 85% of the required mission points to complete a stage, then the price of purchasing this stage will be halved. If you’re near the finish line for a stage and are at 95% progress, then the price will be reduced by five times. For example, if you’ve earned 30,000 mission points, then the price for unlocking this stage will be 499 Golden Eagles. If you’ve earned 33,500 mission points, then you’ll only need 199 Golden Eagles. Keep this in mind if you cannot complete a stage on time![/p][p][/p][h2][b]Tracking your progress[/b][/h2][p align="justify"]You can track the progress of completing stages by clicking on your Nickname > Achievements > Dreams Come True: Mistel. If you don’t manage to complete a stage on time or would like to purchase a stage, you can purchase each stage with Golden Eagles until [b]November 14th[/b] from the Achievements window, which will give you the corresponding rewards.[/p]
